points.title: 音乐启蒙
points.description: 肖邦出生于波兰华沙附近的热拉佐瓦沃拉，6岁时开始学习钢琴，很快展现出非凡的音乐天赋。12岁时，他在华沙国家剧院首次公开演出，演奏了莫扎特的协奏曲。1826年进入华沙音乐学院师从埃尔斯纳，系统学习作曲理论。在此期间，他创作了波兰舞曲、玛祖卡等早期作品，深受波兰民族音乐传统影响。华沙时期奠定了他作为钢琴家和作曲家的基础，同时也培养了他对祖国波兰的深厚感情，这种情感后来成为他创作的重要源泉。
points.descriptionEn: Born near Warsaw in Żelazowa Wola, Chopin began piano studies at age 6 and quickly displayed exceptional musical talent. At 12, he made his public debut at the Warsaw National Theater, performing Mozart's Concerto. In 1826, he entered the Warsaw Conservatory, studying composition with Elsner. During this period, he composed early works including polonaises and mazurkas, deeply influenced by Polish musical traditions. Warsaw established him as both pianist and composer, while fostering his profound connection to Poland, which later became a crucial source of his creative inspiration.

points.title: 流亡起点
points.description: 1830年11月，肖邦离开华沙前往维也纳举行音乐会，途中得知波兰爆发反抗俄国统治的十一月起义。他本想回国参加革命，但被朋友劝阻留在西方。在维也纳，他举办了多场成功的音乐会，但得知起义失败后深受打击。1831年，肖邦创作了革命练习曲，表达了对祖国命运的忧虑和愤怒。这一时期标志着肖邦从波兰音乐家转变为流亡艺术家，他的作品开始融入更强烈的情感表达和对民族命运的思考。
points.descriptionEn: In November 1830, Chopin left Warsaw for Vienna to give concerts, en route learning of the November Uprising against Russian rule in Poland. Though he intended to return and join the revolution, friends persuaded him to remain in the West. In Vienna, he gave several successful concerts, but was deeply affected by news of the uprising's failure. In 1831, he composed the Revolutionary Étude, expressing his anguish and anger over his homeland's fate. This period marked Chopin's transformation from Polish musician to émigré artist, with his works beginning to incorporate stronger emotional expression and reflections on national destiny.

points.title: 巴黎成名
points.description: 1831年底，肖邦抵达巴黎，这座欧洲艺术中心成为他后半生的主要居所。他在巴黎音乐学院举办音乐会，与李斯特、柏辽兹、门德尔松等音乐家交往密切。1835年，肖邦获得法国公民身份。这一时期他创作了包括夜曲、圆舞曲、前奏曲在内的许多代表作，确立了他在巴黎音乐界的地位。肖邦的演奏风格细腻优雅，被誉为'钢琴诗人'，他的作品融合了波兰民族音乐元素与法国精致的艺术传统，开创了钢琴音乐的新风格。
points.descriptionEn: Arriving in Paris in late 1831, this European art center became his main residence for the rest of his life. He performed at the Paris Conservatoire and formed close friendships with musicians like Liszt, Berlioz, and Mendelssohn. In 1835, Chopin obtained French citizenship. During this period, he composed many masterpieces including nocturnes, waltzes, and preludes, establishing his position in Paris's musical world. Chopin's delicate and elegant playing style earned him the title 'Poet of the Piano,' and his works blended Polish national elements with French artistic refinement, creating a new style in piano music.

points.title: 创作巅峰
points.description: 1838年起，肖邦经常前往法国作家乔治·桑的乡村庄园诺昂度假，两人开始了长达九年的关系。在诺昂，肖邦创作了他最成熟的作品，包括叙事曲、谐谑曲、波兰舞曲和奏鸣曲等。这一时期他的音乐风格更加成熟，技巧更加精湛，情感表达更加深刻。1846年，肖邦与乔治·桑关系破裂，对他的创作产生了重大影响。诺昂时期是肖邦创作的黄金时代，他的作品达到了艺术成就的顶峰，对后世钢琴音乐产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: From 1838, Chopin frequently vacationed at Nohant, the country estate of French writer George Sand, with whom he began a nine-year relationship. In Nohant, Chopin composed his most mature works, including ballades, scherzos, polonaises, and sonatas. During this period, his musical style became more refined, his technique more polished, and his emotional expression deeper. In 1846, Chopin's relationship with George Sand ended, significantly impacting his creativity. The Nohant period represented Chopin's golden age of composition, with his works reaching artistic peaks that profoundly influenced future piano music.

points.title: 生命终章
points.description: 1848年欧洲革命爆发，肖邦的健康状况急剧恶化，但仍坚持演出。2月，他在巴黎举办了最后一场音乐会；4月，他前往英国进行短期巡演，在伦敦和曼彻斯特演出。回到巴黎后，肖邦的肺结核病情加重，1849年10月17日在巴黎逝世，享年39岁。临终前，他要求将心脏运回波兰安葬。肖邦的葬礼在巴黎圣母院举行，由李斯特主持，随后安葬于拉雪兹神父公墓。他的去世标志着浪漫主义钢琴音乐一个重要时代的结束，但他的音乐遗产至今仍影响着世界音乐发展。
points.descriptionEn: With the outbreak of the 1848 European revolutions, Chopin's health deteriorated rapidly, though he continued to perform. In February, he gave his last concert in Paris; in April, he undertook a short tour of Britain, performing in London and Manchester. Returning to Paris, Chopin's tuberculosis worsened, and he died on October 17, 1849, at age 39. He requested that his heart be returned to Poland for burial. Chopin's funeral at Notre-Dame de Paris was conducted by Liszt, after which he was buried at Père Lachaise Cemetery. His death marked the end of an important era in Romantic piano music, but his musical legacy continues to influence world music to this day.

appraisal.zh: 肖邦被公认为浪漫主义时期最具特色的钢琴作曲家之一，他把波兰民间音乐元素与法国精致艺术传统熔于一炉，以夜曲、前奏曲、练习曲等作品把精湛技巧与深切情感结合起来，被视为民族浪漫主义的高峰，其作品至今仍是钢琴演奏的黄金标准。也有研究者指出，他专注于钢琴独奏、作品偏于个人化，缺少宏大叙事与社会关怀，流亡中的政治姿态亦受质疑；不过这类意见并未动摇其在音乐史上的核心地位。
appraisal.en: Chopin is widely recognized as one of the most distinctive piano composers of the Romantic era, fusing Polish folk elements with French refinement; his nocturnes, preludes and études combine technical mastery with deep feeling, and he is seen as the peak of national Romanticism, his works remaining the gold standard of piano performance. Some researchers note that his focus on solo piano and personal expression lacks grand narrative and social concern, and question his political stance in exile; such views, however, have not shaken his central place in music history.

supporter.zh: 肖邦被誉为'钢琴诗人'，他将波兰民族精神与浪漫主义完美融合，开创了钢琴音乐的新纪元。他的夜曲、前奏曲、练习曲等作品不仅展现了精湛的技巧，更蕴含着深刻的情感表达。肖邦通过音乐传递了波兰的民族认同和文化尊严，即使在流亡中仍保持对祖国的热爱。他的创新性和艺术成就使他成为音乐史上最具影响力的作曲家之一，对后世钢琴演奏和创作产生了不可估量的影响。
supporter.en: Chopin, hailed as the 'Poet of the Piano,' perfectly merged Polish national spirit with Romanticism, pioneering a new era in piano music. His nocturnes, preludes, and études demonstrate not only technical mastery but profound emotional expression. Through his music, Chopin conveyed Polish national identity and cultural dignity, maintaining his love for his homeland despite exile. His innovation and artistic achievements make him one of history's most influential composers, with an immeasurable impact on future piano performance and composition.

critic.zh: 批评者认为肖邦的作品过于个人化，缺乏社会关怀和宏大叙事。他专注于钢琴独奏形式，被认为限制了音乐的表现范围。此外，肖邦在政治上的保守态度也受到质疑，他虽然热爱祖国，但并未积极参与波兰独立运动，而是选择流亡生活。一些评论家还指出他的音乐技巧华丽但内容肤浅，缺乏贝多芬等作曲家的思想深度。这些批评反映了肖邦作为浪漫主义艺术家在个人表达与社会责任之间的张力。
critic.en: Critics argue that Chopin's work is overly personal, lacking social concern and grand narratives. His focus on solo piano form is seen as limiting musical expression. Additionally, Chopin's conservative political stance is questioned; though he loved his homeland, he did not actively participate in Poland's independence movement, choosing exile instead. Some commentators also note his music's technical brilliance but superficial content, lacking the philosophical depth of composers like Beethoven. These criticisms reflect the tension in Chopin's work between personal expression and social responsibility as a Romantic artist.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，肖邦被定义为浪漫主义时期最具特色的钢琴作曲家之一。他的音乐融合了波兰民间音乐元素与法国精致艺术传统，创造了独特的个人风格。肖邦不仅是技巧大师，更是情感表达的先驱，他的作品至今仍是钢琴演奏的黄金标准。在流行文化中，肖邦被视为忧郁、优雅和天才的象征，他的音乐经常出现在电影、广告等大众媒体中。历史学界认为肖邦代表了民族浪漫主义的高峰，他的音乐既是个人情感的抒发，也是民族文化的载体，体现了19世纪欧洲艺术与政治的复杂交织。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Chopin is defined as one of the most distinctive piano composers of the Romantic period. His music blended Polish folk elements with French artistic refinement, creating a unique personal style. Chopin was not only a master of technique but a pioneer of emotional expression, with his works remaining the gold standard in piano performance. In popular culture, Chopin is symbolized as melancholy, elegance, and genius, with his music frequently appearing in films, advertisements, and other media. Historians consider Chopin to represent the peak of national Romanticism, with his music expressing both personal emotion and serving as a vehicle for national culture, reflecting the complex interweaving of art and politics in 19th-century Europe.

self.zh: 音乐应该像一面镜子，反映出人的内心世界。
self.en: Music should be a mirror reflecting the soul of the people.
